abstract: Efficient two-photon absorption depends on compensating the dispersion of the whole excitation path. Building on established fluorescence-based adjustment, we describe a practical procedure that uses side-view images of fluorescence in a dye cuvette, independently of the microscope's scanning and detection, with reference records, stability warnings and open analysis software. For a 1045 nm laser, maxima lay between 21 and 24 screw turns in 11 of 13 sweeps. For a 920 nm laser, fluorescence maxima at the sample differed by 1.63 kfs^2 on average from autocorrelation minima before the scan optics. The recordings also show limitations from signal instability and proximity to clipping. The procedure targets two-photon microscopes for in vivo imaging, such as of neuronal activity, where tissue heating limits the usable power; it may also apply to photostimulation and polymerisation paths.
